assumptions.reference_input: rho_RB is a pure purification of sigma_B

source_theorem: Barnum-Knill, arXiv:quant-ph/0004088v2, Sec. IV, Theorem 3 Eq. (13), singleton ensemble E={sigma}
map_identity: Barnum-Knill reversal R_{Phi,sigma} is the ordinary Petz adjoint Phi^sharp because Phi(sigma)=sigma.

derived_bound.trace_distance: (1/2)||rho_pur-(id tensor Phi^sharp Phi)(rho_pur)||_1 <= sqrt(1-(1-b_pur)^2) <= sqrt(2 b_pur)

why_not_general_mixed_extension: For a mixed extension rho_RB, b is measured after degrading the purifying reference; trace-distance contractivity only gives b_mixed<=b_pur, so small b_mixed does not bound the purification entanglement fidelity required by Barnum-Knill.
Applying Barnum-Knill instead to id_R tensor Phi with input reference rho_RB makes the transpose map depend on the full rho_RB and generally nonlocal, not id_R tensor Phi^sharp.
Barnum-Knill Theorem 3 averages entanglement fidelity over commuting input ensembles; the paper explicitly leaves the noncommuting-ensemble extension open immediately after Corollary 4.

later_comparison.source: Zheng, He, Lee, Jiang, arXiv:2401.02022v2, Theorem 1 Eqs. (2)-(5), Supplemental Lemma 1 Eq. (S8)
later_comparison.scope: The transpose channel is near-optimal for code-channel fidelity, defined with a purified maximally mixed logical code state.
later_comparison.limitation: This is a full-reference code-space fidelity result, not a bound from the trace residual of an arbitrary mixed extension with marginal sigma.

non_counterexample_scope_check: For sigma=I2/2, Phi=conjugation by Pauli X, and rho=sigma with trivial reference, b=0 and the Petz round trip fixes rho exactly, while Fe(sigma,Phi)=0. This shows mixed-state residual does not imply purification entanglement fidelity; it does not refute the desired round-trip conclusion.
novelty: No novelty or priority inference is made.
